skill.name: gh-stack
skill.description: Manages stacked PRs and splits multi-part work into reviewable branches with gh-stack. Use for stack creation, viewing, edits, push, submit, sync, rebase, merge, or checkout; when asked to split or isolate work for review; whenever a user mentions a stack, branch layers, dependent PRs, or gh stack; or when a stack is checked out.
skill.summary: Plan reviewable branch layers and manage stacked GitHub pull requests with non-interactive gh-stack workflows.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: All 72 static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, ordinary prose, a documentation link, or safe Git command substitutions. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or unauthorized exfiltration in the four reviewed files. The documented workflow still installs an external extension, modifies Git state, and publishes or merges changes through GitHub.

content.value_statement: Large changes become difficult to review when unrelated concerns share one branch. This skill guides dependency-based branch planning and non-interactive stacked PR workflows.
actual_capabilities: Plan linear branch layers by dependency and reviewer concern before implementation.
Guide stack initialization, branch addition, explicit checkout, and navigation.
Use structured stack output to inspect branch ownership, PR state, and rebase needs.
Push branches and submit linked draft or review-ready pull requests through gh-stack.
Guide synchronization, cascade rebasing, conflict recovery, and optional pruning of merged local branches.
Scope stack merges and explain worktree ownership, merge queues, and external-tool linking.
limitations: Requires Git 2.36 or later, an authenticated GitHub CLI, and the gh-stack extension.
Submitting stacked PRs requires stacked pull requests to be enabled on the repository.
Stacks are linear; parallel work requires separate stacks.
Interactive modify, switch, and in-place reordering are not available through non-interactive workflows.

use_cases.title: Split a Feature Into Reviewable Layers
use_cases.description: Plan schema, API, and interface branches in dependency order, then submit a linked set of draft pull requests.

use_cases.title: Update a Shared Lower Layer
use_cases.description: Find the branch that owns a change, commit there, and rebase dependent branches while respecting worktree ownership.

use_cases.title: Automate Stack Maintenance
use_cases.description: Use explicit targets, structured output, remote selection, and documented recovery paths to maintain stacks without interactive menus.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an Existing Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my current gh-stack state. Summarize branch order, pull request status, and rebase needs without changing branches or publishing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a New Feature Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a stack for [feature]. Propose dependency-ordered branches using repository naming conventions. Explain each review scope and wait for approval before creating branches.

prompt_templates.title: Edit the Correct Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Place [change] in its owning branch. Inspect ownership and worktree state, propose targeted staging and upstack rebasing, and request approval before remote updates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: modify an existing dependency layer.

prompt_templates.title: Recover and Publish a Diverged Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose divergence between my local and GitHub stacks. Compare both chains, explain recovery options, and preserve branches. Await approval before regrouping or publishing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: reconcile stack metadata and remote state.

output_examples.input: I changed API code while working on the frontend branch.
output: Inspect stack state and file history to identify the owning API layer.
Move to the correct owning worktree and stage only the API change.
After committing, rebase dependent branches and verify the stack before requesting approval to push.

best_practices: Plan branch dependencies before implementation and stage only the files belonging to each layer.
Select the intended remote explicitly and review publication or merge scope before approving remote changes.
Use structured view output, verify exit status, and resolve conflicts in the reported owning worktree.
anti_patterns: Implement every concern on one branch and expect stack metadata alone to split or reorder commits.
Invoke interactive menus from automation or parse human-readable status messages as structured stack state.
Assume exit code zero proves synchronization completed when the output reports Sync aborted.

faq.question: What must be installed before using this skill?
faq.answer: Install Git 2.36 or later, authenticate GitHub CLI, and install the gh-stack extension. The skill provides guidance rather than the extension implementation.

faq.question: Can Claude and Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Command execution requires a compatible environment with the necessary tools and repository access.

faq.question: Does pushing a stack create pull requests?
faq.answer: No. Push updates active branches. Submit pushes branches, creates missing pull requests, and links them into a GitHub stack.

faq.question: Are new pull requests drafts?
faq.answer: Submit creates draft pull requests by default. The open flag marks new and existing pull requests ready for review.

faq.question: Can this skill reorder branches without interaction?
faq.answer: There is no non-interactive in-place reorder. Correct Git ancestry first, then rebuild stack tracking; metadata changes alone do not reorder commits.

faq.question: Does this workflow change local or remote data?
faq.answer: Yes. Commands can install an extension, configure Git, rewrite history, publish branches, merge PRs, and prune merged local branches when explicitly requested.
